rationale: This is a one-operator swap (MA→TS_MIN) on the archive's existing "Persistent Fixed Charge Coverage Regime" expression, so despite a coherent tail-risk rationale it is a cosmetic variant whose payoff is largely predictable from the two parents already in the archive.

target_name: Commitment Coverage Net Of External Raising
rationale: Internally consistent and sign-coherent, but a rank-sum of two already-tested legs (one of which, gross issuance-to-assets, is essentially the published external-financing anomaly) is close to a mechanical blend whose result will likely interpolate the two parents rather than reveal a new mechanism.

The COALESCE(oancf, ib+dp) substitution is a legitimate and economically defensible sample-extension of two near-identical archive signals rather than a coverage hack, but the mechanism is unchanged so the informational value is confined to sample-robustness rather than a new source of return predictability.

target_name: Worst Year Coverage Of Total Distributions
rationale: Adding prstkc to the archive's worst-year dividend coverage is a single-term perturbation, and the stated hypothesis is explicitly agnostic about direction ("if X it weakens, if Y it strengthens"), which contradicts the declared positive expected sign and makes this a diagnostic probe rather than a signal proposal.

target_name: Share Of Reported Profit Surviving Commitments
rationale: Deflating by |MA(ib,3)| makes the statistic dominated by the operating-cash-flow-to-earnings ratio — i.e. the published accruals anomaly — and the absolute-value denominator is unstable near zero earnings and destroys the sign interpretation for loss-makers, so extreme scores will be driven by tiny denominators rather than by large post-commitment surplus.

Internally consistent with the negative sign, but it is simply the gen-7 short-side winner with dltis deleted from the issuance leg, and the residual equity-issuance component is itself the well-documented net-stock-issues anomaly, so the incremental learning is a channel attribution rather than a new signal.
